requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1.
requirements.summary: The final state directly shows active LV data_vg/data_lv mounted read-write at /srv/data, including successful recovery after restart.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB while it remains mounted.
requirements.summary: The LV and XFS filesystem grew from 1 GiB to 2 GiB online. Before and after observations retain mount ID 119 and device 252:0; the final block-device size is 2,147,483,648 bytes.

requirements.requirement: Keep the mounted volume's contents intact during growth.
requirements.summary: The marker and 8 MiB payload have identical SHA-256 hashes before growth, after growth, and after restart; post-restart writing also succeeds.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 are unchanged before and after execution. Signed EL7 x86_64 LVM packages were installed successfully and demonstrated working storage operations and reboot recovery.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct transition evidence. The required node1 restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledged reboot, a different post-restart boot ID corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered service, mount, LV, data integrity, and system health are shown.
limitations: Native package-manager consistency checks timed out in both lifecycle snapshots, so overall RPM database consistency was not independently observed.
The lifecycle collector did not capture task-specific storage state; final storage conclusions rely on the detailed executor command evidence.
Several downloaded RPMs and the imported-key file remain under /tmp, reducing operational hygiene but not demonstrated functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unrelated or unjustified state-changing mutation is established. Package installation, loop-device setup, persistent activation, test-data creation, and reboot were causally connected to delivering or validating the outcome; restarting rhsmcertd restored the post-reboot health state. The sole hygiene defect is retained download residue: the CentOS signing key and six RPM files created under /tmp were not removed and remained in the final lifecycle snapshot. No reverted unnecessary mutation was identified.
